neighbours.label: ' offensive' as a military noun (take the offensive, go on the offensive, launch an offensive); not the adjective meaning insulting, and only weakly other combat nouns (attack, engagements)
fire: By early June the Red Army was ready to go on the offensive in the south.

The rebels went on the offensive after the rains ended.
Supplies ran short and the spring offensive stalled near the border.
Both corps were ordered to resume the offensive toward the capital.
The allies opened a major offensive on the eastern bank in August.
quiet: By early June the Red Army was ready to dig in along the south bank.
